name: Two block haircut

card.summary: A men's cut with clipped short sides and back and a longer top, common in Korean styling, that frames the face and gives volume and shape to the top.
card.aka: two-block cut; two block; undercut (English term)
card.note: Needs regular trims to keep the contrast between sections.

quick.overview:
The two-block cut leaves hair on the top and front longer while the sides and back are clipped short, so the hair looks divided into two parts. It is a basic men's style that is widely worn in South Korea and Japan under this name.

It helps looks by emphasising the face and jawline, adding perceived volume on top and giving a neat outline. Longer front hair can be styled forward, to the side or swept up.
quick.how: A barber clips the sides and back short and leaves the top and front longer, sometimes with a visible step between the sections. Wearers style the top with wax or pomade or leave it natural. Korean versions more often keep longer front hair, according to the Korean Wikipedia entry. The cut is maintained with regular trims as the sides grow out.
quick.risks: There is no medical risk beyond ordinary hair-cutting concerns. The Korean Wikipedia entry notes some schools in South Korea have restricted the style, which has been debated. Results depend on hair type and the barber.

lead: The two-block haircut is a men's cut in which the lower portion of the hair is clipped short while the upper portion is left longer, so a visible step forms and the hair appears to be in two blocks.[1] The name is used in Korea and Japan; the Korean Wikipedia article says the English-language equivalent is the undercut.[1]

The undercut is defined in English as a hairstyle where hair is shaved along a line above the ears, with the top kept long. Its history includes early-20th-century working-class styles, a revival in the early 2010s with longer, swept-back or pomaded tops, and centrally parted versions.[2]
As an appearance tool, the cut puts attention on the face and creates height and volume on top while keeping the sides neat. No published studies examine it.

chain: Longer top gains visible shape and volume
Face and jawline look more defined and tidy
angle.text: The short sides expose the face and ears and create contrast with a fuller top. People choose it for a clean outline that can be styled forward, sideways or up.

infobox: Short sides and back, longer top

paras: Korean Wikipedia describes the cut as one where the lower half of the hair is clipped short and the upper half left longer, leaving the top and front intact. It describes the style as Western in origin and a basic men's cut there, and adds that in Western countries it is often swept up with wax or pomade while Korean versions more often keep longer front hair.[1]

English Wikipedia lists the undercut's history: popular in the early 1900s, mainstream in the 1920s to 1940s, overtaken by longer styles from the 1960s, revived in the late 1980s as a centrally parted variant and in the early 2010s with longer, swept-back or slicked tops.[2] It does not describe the Korean two-block cut separately.[2]
In Korea the style has been a school-dress-code topic, with some schools banning it and the issue debated as a matter of student rights.[1] Some women in Korea adopted it from the late 2010s.[1]

timeline.event: Undercut revived in English-speaking countries with longer, swept-back tops.[2]
Some women in Korea adopt the two-block cut.[1]
